Repeated sink removal in a finite DAG removes every non-original-source: each remaining non-source eventually loses all unprocessed outgoing edges while indegree stays positive until source processing. Original sources remain in their initial FIFO source queue because the sink-add test requires indegree>0. Therefore after both queue loops no unprocessed node remains; chooseNodeWithMaxOutflow is unreachable.

With k original sources, they receive positive1..k in original source-queue order. The other n-k nodes receive negative-1..-(n-k), then shift n+1 -> k+1..n. For every edge source mark<target mark because targets are sink-removed before predecessors, or predecessor is an original source. No reversal or CYCLIC write occurs. Singleton isolated node is an initial sink and shifts to1.

All degree updates are unit decrements for incident edges of a removed node, skip already marked neighbors and preserve port incoming-before-outgoing order. In the sink-drain phase indegrees of remaining nodes do not decrease, so each positive-outdegree node reaches0 at one update and is queued once; original sources are excluded from sink insertion.
